name: Crucible Industries Longstrike LS-15 'Causeway'
description:
A modular precision rifle system that can be configured for ranges from 500 to 6,000 meters by swapping barrel assemblies, optics packages, and ammunition types. The Longstrike is Crucible's answer to operators who need a single platform capable of adapting to any engagement scenario.

The LS-15's core receiver accepts three barrel configurations: a conventional 7.62mm precision barrel for urban work, a heavy .408 barrel for extended range, and an electromagnetic accelerator barrel powered by an auxiliary capacitor pack. Each configuration changes the weapon's characteristics entirely, and experienced operators can swap barrels in under 90 seconds.

Crucible sells the Longstrike as a complete system — rifle, three barrels, optics suite, and a hardened transit case. The full kit costs more than most operators earn in a year, but those who own one rarely carry anything else.
legality: Licensed — military and corporate security contractors
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm / .408 / 4mm electromagnetic (barrel-dependent)
effective_range: 500-6,000 meters (configuration-dependent)
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic (7.62mm), bolt-action (.408), single-shot (EM)
capacity: 10 / 5 / 3 rounds (configuration-dependent)
weight: 5.8-11.2 kg (configuration-dependent)
power_source: None (conventional) / Auxiliary capacitor (EM barrel)
tactical_use: The Causeway's modularity makes it the preferred platform for operators who deploy across multiple environments without logistical support. A contractor moving from a Tier 2 urban extraction to a Tier 5 border interdiction can reconfigure the same weapon for both missions. The electromagnetic barrel turns the platform into a lightweight railgun sniper capable of defeating armored targets, though the auxiliary power requirement limits its sustained use.
cultural_context: Crucible's marketing for the Longstrike emphasizes self-reliance and adaptability — values that resonate with GLMZ's independent contractor culture. Owning a complete LS-15 kit is a professional credential. Fixers who see a Causeway case know they are dealing with someone who takes precision work seriously and has the resources to prove it.
story_hooks: An LS-15 electromagnetic barrel was found at a crime scene with its serial numbers intact — it traces to a Crucible demonstration kit that was supposed to be destroyed after a failed field test. Someone inside Crucible is diverting prototype equipment.
A contractor has modified their Causeway to accept a fourth barrel type — a plasma-channeled accelerator that nobody has seen before. They are offering demonstrations to interested parties.

physical_description.visual_profile: A skeletal, purposeful sniper platform with an exposed modular architecture. The Causeway reads as deliberately unadorned — all function, zero flourish. Its receiver is a precision-machined spine of dark alloy from which barrel assemblies, stock, and rail systems attach with surgical precision. The weapon has an almost architectural quality: clean lines, pronounced negative space, and an aggressive forward cant that suggests perpetual readiness.
physical_description.dimensions: Base receiver: 48 cm. Total length varies: 7.62mm configuration 118 cm, .408 configuration 134 cm, EM barrel 112 cm. Barrel assemblies themselves 38-52 cm depending on variant. Width across rail system: 8 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: The 7.62mm configuration feels balanced and almost elegant in the shoulder — 5.8 kg distributed across a long sight plane. The .408 feels genuinely hefty, a brute instrument requiring respect and proper positioning. The EM barrel configuration, despite being lighter at the muzzle, feels dense and front-loaded due to the auxiliary capacitor pack mounted forward of the receiver — approximately 8.4 kg of purpose.
physical_description.primary_material: Receiver and rail system: aerospace-grade titanium-aluminum composite with diamond-hard anodizing. Barrel assemblies: chrome-moly steel for conventional barrels, electromagnetic coils wrapped in carbon-reinforced polymer for the EM variant. Stock: modular carbon composite, tool-free attachment points.
physical_description.finish: Receiver and rails: deep charcoal anodize with mil-spec satin finish — no shine, designed to kill reflections. Barrel assemblies wear a matte nitride finish in gunmetal grey. The auxiliary capacitor pack features brushed industrial grey with subtle heat-dissipation ridging. All attachment points show precision machine marks — no polishing, no cosmetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: military charcoal and gun-metal grey across the platform. Accents: white manufacturer stamps, pale blue LED indicators on the capacitor pack (visible when powered), and faint amber witness marks on quick-disconnect joints. Orange caution striping on the EM barrel's muzzle shroud.
physical_description.grip_texture: Pistol grip: cross-hatched rubberized polymer with aggressive texturing for gloved operation. Wraparound texture extends to the rail panels. The barrel quick-disconnect collars are bare, knurled steel for ungloved manipulation in the field.
distinctive_features: Quick-release barrel mounting system with tool-free indexing — three prominent alignment lugs visible on receiver face
Modular top rail: Picatinny 20mm system spanning the entire receiver, slightly elevated for optics clearance
Auxiliary capacitor pack mounted forward of receiver (EM configuration only) — cylindrical, ribbed for heat dissipation, with small indicator LEDs
Witness holes and calibration marks visible on each barrel assembly, color-coded to configuration type
Precision-drilled gas ports along the conventional barrels, catching light subtly
Charging handle positioned amidships on the receiver, oversized and angled for gloved operation
Three-point stock attachment with locking indicators — minimal sag, surgical precision
Forward assist button with sharp, angular geometry — no rounded edges, pure function
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES stamped in small sans-serif lettering on the left receiver face, just aft of the ejection port. Serial plate mounted on the right side: brushed stainless, legible from field distance. Each barrel assembly bears its caliber designation in white paint: '7.62×51', '.408 CHEY TAC', '4MM EM' respectively. Model number 'LS-15' laser-etched on the lower receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-fresh examples show pristine anodize with perfect witness mark clarity. Field-used Causeways develop subtle wear: scuffing on the capacitor pack from transit cases, fine scratches on the rail system from scope mounting/remounting, and occasional carbon fouling around the barrel indexing points. Well-maintained contractor weapons show meticulous cleaning with zero rust, though the matte finish hides dust and minor marks deliberately. Heavily-used EM configurations show heat discoloration on the capacitor shroud — a badge of sustained engagement.
